doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

title: Sunday parades in Algiers and the first parade Martin saw
summary: Russell asks about parades on the Algiers side. Martin says they were usually held on Sundays, remembers the first parade at Teche and Newton, and lists clubs such as Eagle Eye and the Odd Fellows.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Did they have many parades across the river? In those old days? Yeah. Or mostly just funerals? Or were there other parades too?
There were parades too. All of them, yeah. There were parades too.
And would have them on Sunday like they do nowadays. That's right. They usually have them on Sundays.

That's right. They have them on Sundays. The first parade I seen was the last small boy and left... Tash and Newton there. The parade? Yeah. Well, they usually have parades every Sunday. I'm talking about the first parade I seen Tash and Newton. Where, in IJ? Yeah. Well, I never remember no parade in IJ. All the parades most used to be over here.
Well that's with them clubs, but they had parades over there before the bulls and lions and them was up.
Yeah, I don't remember no parades anymore. What were some of the old clubs over there? I remember there was a turtle back, all eagle eye, they're still there.
Eagle eye, yeah, the eagle eye, the young men, all of them used to parade, used to have parades. You take the odd fella, they used to parade. Now you take...
Is there any masons over there? Yeah, they used to parade. They used to parade over here though.
